steps.title: Prepare RNA elution buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 200 µL of 1 M Na‑MOPS (pH 6.0), 1 200 µL of 5 M NaCl, and 40 µL of 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0); add nuclease‑free water to a final volume of 20 mL.

steps.title: Prepare 10× TAE buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 48.5 g Trizma® base (400 mM) in water, add 11.4 mL glacial acetic acid (17.4 M) and 20 mL of 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) (10 mM final); bring the volume to 1 L with nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Isolate synthetic circRNA (gel extraction)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 %–2 % agarose gel containing GelRed®, mix circRNA with 2× RNA loading dye, load ≥100 ng per well, run at 90 V until the dye front reaches three‑quarters of the gel, visualize under UV, excise the circRNA band.

steps.title: Extract circRNA from gel
steps.instruction: Crush the gel slice with a pestle, add 2 volumes of RNA elution buffer (e.g., 200 µL buffer to 100 mg gel), incubate at room temperature ≥30 min (or overnight at 4 °C); optionally filter through a 0.22 µm syringe filter and ethanol‑precipitate for storage.

steps.title: Isolate total cellular RNA (TRIzol)
steps.instruction: Aspirate media from 80 % confluent HEK293T cells in a T‑75 flask, add 7.5 mL TRIzol (1 mL per 10 cm²), pipette gently to lyse cells, follow the manufacturer’s TRIzol protocol, resuspend RNA in 50 µL nuclease‑free water, measure concentration on a Nanodrop, assess integrity on a 1 % agarose gel (28S/18S bands).

steps.title: Remove linear RNA with RNase R
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL RNase R to 20 µg RNA in a total volume of 20 µL, incubate 37 °C for 30 min, clean up with a Zymo RNA Clean and Concentrator‑25 column, elute in 25–50 µL nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Design reverse‑transcription primer
steps.instruction: Design an RT primer that anneals ≥100 nt upstream of the circRNA junction and does not overlap the junction.

steps.title: Prepare RNA primer mix
steps.instruction: In a PCR tube combine 2 µL of 1 µM RT primer, 1–3 µL circRNA template (1 pg–1 µg), 1 µL 10 mM each dNTP mix, and nuclease‑free water to a total of 6 µL; heat at 95 °C for 30 s, then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare uMRT master mix (14 µL per sample)
steps.instruction: Mix 1 µL nuclease‑free water, 7 µL 2× RT reaction buffer, 1 µL UltraMarathonRT (20 U/µL, giving 1 U/µL final), 1 µL RNaseOUT (40 U/µL), and 1 µL High Boost; total volume 14 µL.

steps.title: Perform reverse transcription
steps.instruction: Combine 14 µL uMRT master mix with 6 µL RNA primer mix (total 20 µL); run thermocycler 20 °C for 15 min (first‑strand synthesis), 95 °C for 1 min (inactivation), then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Design divergent PCR primers
steps.instruction: Design a forward and reverse primer pair that are divergent, adjacent, and each ≥100 nt from the circRNA junction; the reverse primer may be the same as the RT primer.

steps.title: Set up PCR amplification
steps.instruction: In a 50 µL reaction combine 22 µL water, 25 µL 2× DreamTaq Master Mix, 1 µL cDNA template (1–100 ng/µL), 1 µL 10 µM forward primer, and 1 µL 10 µM reverse primer.

steps.title: Run PCR thermocycling
steps.instruction: Thermocycler program: 98 °C 30 s initial denature; 30–40 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, annealing at (Tm − 5) °C 30 s, 72 °C extension 1 min per kb (add 1 min per kb for amplicons >2 kb); final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold.

steps.title: Analyze PCR products by gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 % agarose gel containing GelRed®, load 2–6 µL of each PCR product, run, and visualize under UV (GelDoc Go). Adjust gel percentage if amplicon size differs.

steps.title: Clean up PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: Purify PCR products using the DNA Clean and Concentrator‑25 kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol; measure purified DNA concentration on a Nanodrop.

steps.title: Sanger sequencing (≤500 bp amplicons)
steps.instruction: Submit 15 µL of purified PCR product at ≥50 ng/µL with an appropriate sequencing primer to a commercial Sanger sequencing service.

steps.title: Nanopore sequencing (>500 bp amplicons)
steps.instruction: Submit 10 µL of purified PCR product at 20–200 ng/µL for commercial nanopore sequencing; follow vendor‑specific instructions.

description: Validation of protocol uMRT produces large circRNA concatemers We initially evaluated the RT-PCR method using a small circRNA encoding a 114 nucleotide (nt) 3xFLAG sequence. The circular 3xFLAG sequence and all primers used in RT-PCR are found in Dataset S1. Details of the synthesis of the 3xFLAG circRNA sequence are provided in a previous publication by Du et al. [7]. We performed reverse transcription of this circRNA using iScript, SuperScript III (SSIII), and uMRT, followed by PCR amplification of the cDNA products with divergent primers ( Figure 2A ). Less than 2 ng of RNA template (below the Nanodrop detection limit) was used for reverse transcription. 1 µL of the reverse transcription reaction was used as template for the PCR reactions as described in section D. The RT-PCR products from SSIII and uMRT were large concatemers of the circRNA, which was validated by Sanger sequencing ( Figure 2C ). iScript, which has an active RNase H domain, produced cDNA that was 1–2 times the size of the circRNA, which is under the minimum 150 nt length required for Sanger sequencing with most commercial services. In contrast, SSIII displayed higher processivity, generating a ladder pattern, whereas uMRT showed even greater processivity, producing cDNA concatemers that were 10–20 times the size of the original circRNA ( Figure 1A ). Despite the presence of multiple PCR products in both SSIII and uMRT samples, these products were suitable for Sanger sequencing, as they represent repeats of the same sequence ( Figure 2C , Dataset S1). We further examined the capability of uMRT to perform rolling circle reverse transcription at lower temperatures. uMRT successfully synthesized cDNA from the 3xFLAG template at room temperature (25 °C), 30 °C, and 42 °C ( Figure 2B ).
